lesson.text: Quick memory: how many beats does a crotchet last? (1 beat: ta.) In grade 3 you read crotchets, quavers and rests. Today: longer notes, and how notes fill a bar.
A semibreve (a whole note) lasts 4 beats: an open note head with no stem. Say ta-a-a-a, and hold it.
A minim (a half note) lasts 2 beats: an open head with a stem. Say ta-a. Two minims last as long as one semibreve.
A crotchet (a quarter note) lasts 1 beat, and two quavers (eighth notes) share 1 beat. So 1 semibreve lasts as long as 2 minims, or 4 crotchets, or 8 quavers.
The US names are fractions of a whole note: half, quarter, eighth. A minim is half as long as a semibreve, and a crotchet a quarter as long.
Bars group the beats. In 4/4 time, every bar holds 4 crotchet beats: one semibreve, or two minims, or a minim and two crotchets, or …
Worked example: a minim, a crotchet and two quavers: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 beats, a full bar of 4/4.
Try it in the world: build a rhythm path in your world: a long block for each minim and a short block for each crotchet. Walk along it saying ta-a and ta. Next: beats in a bar.

exercises.hint: An open head with no stem at all.
An open head with a stem.

exercises.prompt: How many beats does a minim last?
Listen: four short notes show the beat, then one long note. How long is the long note?
exercises.hint: Tap the beat with the short notes, and keep tapping through the long one.
exercises.explain: The long note lasts as long as the four short ones: 4 beats, a semibreve.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last altogether?
exercises.hint: Say ta-a for each minim and count.
exercises.explain: 2 + 2 = 4 beats: as long as a semibreve.

exercises.prompt: Two minims last as long as one semibreve.
exercises.explain: True: 2 + 2 = 4 beats, the same as a semibreve.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last altogether?
exercises.hint: A minim is 2 beats and a crotchet 1.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last altogether?
exercises.hint: A semibreve is 4 beats and a minim 2.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy this rhythm: a minim, then two crotchets.
exercises.hint: Each beat has two boxes. A crotchet claps in the first box; a minim claps once and waits 3 more boxes.
exercises.explain: You heard ta-a, ta, ta: claps in boxes 1, 5 and 7.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy this rhythm: a crotchet, a minim, a crotchet.
exercises.hint: Each beat has two boxes. A crotchet claps in the first box; a minim claps once and waits 3 more boxes.
exercises.explain: You heard ta, ta-a, ta: claps in boxes 1, 3 and 7.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which note is longer, the first or the second?
exercises.hint: Count the beats while each note sounds.
exercises.explain: The first note lasts 2 beats and the second 4: the second is longer.

exercises.prompt: Match each note to how long it lasts.
exercises.hint: Each note lasts twice as long as the next one down.
exercises.explain: Semibreve 4, minim 2, crotchet 1, quaver half a beat.

exercises.prompt: Put these notes in order, shortest first.
exercises.hint: Think of their US names: eighth, quarter, half, whole.
exercises.explain: Quaver (half a beat), crotchet (1), minim (2), semibreve (4).

exercises.prompt: How many quavers last as long as one minim?
exercises.hint: How many quavers fit in one beat? How many beats is a minim?
exercises.explain: 2 quavers make 1 beat, and a minim is 2 beats: 2 × 2 = 4 quavers.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last altogether?
exercises.hint: Dotted minim 3, crotchet 1, two quavers 1, minim 2.

exercises.prompt: This 4/4 bar needs one more note. Which one fits the gap?
exercises.hint: Count the beats already in the bar. How many are missing?
exercises.explain: A minim (2) and two quavers (1) make 3 beats, so 1 is missing: a crotchet.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then copy this rhythm: a minim, two quavers, a crotchet.
exercises.hint: Each beat has two boxes. A crotchet claps in the first box; a minim claps once and waits 3 more boxes.
exercises.explain: You heard ta-a, ti-ti, ta: claps in boxes 1, 5, 6 and 7.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which rhythm did you hear?
exercises.hint: Clap along with the sound. Which picture matches where the long note comes?
exercises.explain: You heard ta-a, ta, ta: a minim, then two crotchets.

exercises.prompt: A crotchet is called a quarter note because it lasts a quarter as long as a semibreve.
exercises.hint: How many crotchets fit in a semibreve?
exercises.explain: True: 4 crotchets fill a semibreve, so each is a quarter of it.

play.hook: The drums have lost their rhythm. Listen, then play it back beat by beat!
coach: A semibreve lasts 4 beats: hold it.
A crotchet lasts 1 beat; two quavers share one.
In 4/4 time, every bar holds 4 beats.
play.world_task: Build a rhythm path: a long block for each minim, a short block for each crotchet. Walk it saying ta-a and ta.
